namespace App\Providers\Filament;

use BezhanSalleh\FilamentShield\FilamentShieldPlugin;
use Filament\Http\Middleware\Authenticate;
use Filament\Http\Middleware\AuthenticateSession;
use Filament\Http\Middleware\DisableBladeIconComponents;
use Filament\Http\Middleware\DispatchServingFilamentEvent;
use Filament\Pages\Dashboard;
use Filament\Panel;
use Filament\PanelProvider;
use Filament\Support\Colors\Color;
use Filament\Widgets\AccountWidget;
use Filament\Widgets\FilamentInfoWidget;
use Illuminate\Cookie\Middleware\AddQueuedCookiesToResponse;
use Illuminate\Cookie\Middleware\EncryptCookies;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Http\Middleware\PreventRequestForgery;
use Illuminate\Routing\Middleware\SubstituteBindings;
use Illuminate\Session\Middleware\StartSession;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\View\Middleware\ShareErrorsFromSession;
use Livewire\Livewire;

class AdminPanelProvider extends PanelProvider
{
    public function boot(): void
    {
        /**
         * this fixes the issue with nginx server, where livewire.js is not found
         * (removing the dot forces nginx to follow the route and to not serve it as static file)
         * @see https://benjamincrozat.com/livewire-js-404-not-found
         * @see https://laracasts.com/discuss/channels/livewire/has-anyone-got-livewire-3-running-in-production-on-a-nginx-server
         */
        Livewire::setScriptRoute(function ($handle) {
            // @phpstan-ignore argument.type (su $handle)
            return Route::get('/livewire/livewirejs', $handle);
        });
    }

    public function panel(Panel $panel): Panel
    {
        return $panel
            ->default()
            ->id('admin')
            ->path('admin')
            ->login()
            ->passwordReset()
            ->colors([
                'primary' => Color::Amber,
            ])
            ->viteTheme('resources/css/filament/admin/theme.css')
            ->discoverResources(in: app_path('Filament/Resources'), for: 'App\Filament\Resources')
            ->discoverPages(in: app_path('Filament/Pages'), for: 'App\Filament\Pages')
            ->pages([
                Dashboard::class,
            ])
            ->discoverWidgets(in: app_path('Filament/Widgets'), for: 'App\Filament\Widgets')
            ->widgets([
                AccountWidget::class,
                FilamentInfoWidget::class,
            ])
            ->middleware([
                EncryptCookies::class,
                AddQueuedCookiesToResponse::class,
                StartSession::class,
                AuthenticateSession::class,
                ShareErrorsFromSession::class,
                PreventRequestForgery::class,
                SubstituteBindings::class,
                DisableBladeIconComponents::class,
                DispatchServingFilamentEvent::class,
            ])
            ->plugins([
                FilamentShieldPlugin::make(),
            ])
            ->authMiddleware([
                Authenticate::class,
            ]);
    }
}

namespace App\Providers\Filament;

use App\Filament\Resources\AdminResource;

use Filament\Panel;
use Filament\PanelProvider;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Event;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage;
use Spatie\MediaLibrary\ResponsiveImages\Events\ResponsiveImagesGeneratedEvent;

/**
 * Admin panel provider for the site.
 * Uses the default configuration from the filament-helper package.
 */
class AdminPanelProvider extends PanelProvider
{
    public function panel(Panel $panel): Panel
    {

        PanelDefaults::make($panel);

        // add further customizations here...

        /**
         * AdminResource usa User come modello, ma i permessi Shield devono
         * usare 'Admin' come entità (non 'User') per distinguerli.
         */
        FilamentShield::buildPermissionKeyUsing(
            function (string $entity, string $affix, string $subject, string $case, string $separator): string {
                if ($entity === AdminResource::class) {
                    $subject = 'Admin';
                }

                return FilamentShield::defaultPermissionKeyBuilder(
                    affix: $affix,
                    separator: $separator,
                    subject: $subject,
                    case: $case,
                );
            }
        );

        if (config('filament-helper.tinify.enabled')) {
            $this->registerImageOptimizationJob();
        }

        return $panel;

    }

    protected function registerImageOptimizationJob(): void
    {
        Event::listen(
            ResponsiveImagesGeneratedEvent::class,
            function (ResponsiveImagesGeneratedEvent $event) {

                // loop thorught responsive images and build path for each of them, then dispatch the job to optimize the image
                foreach ($event->media->responsive_images as $conversionName) {

                    foreach ($conversionName['urls'] as $relativePath) {
                        $imagePath = Storage::disk($event->media->disk)->path(implode('/', [
                            $event->media->id,
                            'responsive-images',
                            $relativePath
                        ]));

                        OptimizeImage::dispatch($imagePath);

                    }
                }
            }
        );

    }

}

class AdminPanelProvider extends PanelProvider

    public function boot(): void
    {
        /**
         * this fixes the issue with nginx server, where livewire.js is not found
         * (removing the dot forces nginx to follow the route and to not serve it as static file)
         * @see https://benjamincrozat.com/livewire-js-404-not-found
         * @see https://laracasts.com/discuss/channels/livewire/has-anyone-got-livewire-3-running-in-production-on-a-nginx-server
         */
        Livewire::setScriptRoute(function ($handle) {
            // @phpstan-ignore argument.type (su $handle)
            return Route::get('/livewire/livewirejs', $handle);
        });
    }

    public function panel(Panel $panel): Panel
    {

        PanelDefaults::make($panel);

        // add further customizations here...

        /**
         * AdminResource usa User come modello, ma i permessi Shield devono
         * usare 'Admin' come entità (non 'User') per distinguerli.
         */
        FilamentShield::buildPermissionKeyUsing(
            function (string $entity, string $affix, string $subject, string $case, string $separator): string {
                if ($entity === AdminResource::class) {
                    $subject = 'Admin';
                }

                return FilamentShield::defaultPermissionKeyBuilder(
                    affix: $affix,
                    separator: $separator,
                    subject: $subject,
                    case: $case,
                );
            }
        );

        if (config('filament-helper.tinify.enabled')) {
            $this->registerImageOptimizationJob();
        }

        return $panel;

    }

    protected function registerImageOptimizationJob(): void
    {
        Event::listen(
            ResponsiveImagesGeneratedEvent::class,
            function (ResponsiveImagesGeneratedEvent $event) {

                // loop thorught responsive images and build path for each of them, then dispatch the job to optimize the image
                foreach ($event->media->responsive_images as $conversionName) {

                    foreach ($conversionName['urls'] as $relativePath) {
                        $imagePath = Storage::disk($event->media->disk)->path(implode('/', [
                            $event->media->id,
                            'responsive-images',
                            $relativePath
                        ]));

                        OptimizeImage::dispatch($imagePath);

                    }
                }
            }
        );

    }

}

<?php

namespace App\Providers\Filament;

use App\Filament\Resources\AdminResource;
use AtrioTeam\FilamentHelper\Jobs\OptimizeImage;
use AtrioTeam\FilamentHelper\PanelDefaults;
use BezhanSalleh\FilamentShield\Facades\FilamentShield;
use Filament\Panel;
use Filament\PanelProvider;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Event;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage;
use Livewire\Livewire;
use Spatie\MediaLibrary\ResponsiveImages\Events\ResponsiveImagesGeneratedEvent;

/**
 * Admin panel provider for the site.
 * Uses the default configuration from the filament-helper package.
 */
class AdminPanelProvider extends PanelProvider
{
    public function boot(): void
    {
        /**
         * this fixes the issue with nginx server, where livewire.js is not found
         * (removing the dot forces nginx to follow the route and to not serve it as static file)
         * @see https://benjamincrozat.com/livewire-js-404-not-found
         * @see https://laracasts.com/discuss/channels/livewire/has-anyone-got-livewire-3-running-in-production-on-a-nginx-server
         */
        Livewire::setScriptRoute(function ($handle) {
            // @phpstan-ignore argument.type (su $handle)
            return Route::get('/livewire/livewirejs', $handle);
        });
    }

    public function panel(Panel $panel): Panel
    {

        PanelDefaults::make($panel);

        // add further customizations here...

        /**
         * AdminResource usa User come modello, ma i permessi Shield devono
         * usare 'Admin' come entità (non 'User') per distinguerli.
         */
        FilamentShield::buildPermissionKeyUsing(
            function (string $entity, string $affix, string $subject, string $case, string $separator): string {
                if ($entity === AdminResource::class) {
                    $subject = 'Admin';
                }

                return FilamentShield::defaultPermissionKeyBuilder(
                    affix: $affix,
                    separator: $separator,
                    subject: $subject,
                    case: $case,
                );
            }
        );

        if (config('filament-helper.tinify.enabled')) {
            $this->registerImageOptimizationJob();
        }

        return $panel;

    }

    protected function registerImageOptimizationJob(): void
    {
        Event::listen(
            ResponsiveImagesGeneratedEvent::class,
            function (ResponsiveImagesGeneratedEvent $event) {

                // loop thorught responsive images and build path for each of them, then dispatch the job to optimize the image
                foreach ($event->media->responsive_images as $conversionName) {

                    foreach ($conversionName['urls'] as $relativePath) {
                        $imagePath = Storage::disk($event->media->disk)->path(implode('/', [
                            $event->media->id,
                            'responsive-images',
                            $relativePath
                        ]));

                        OptimizeImage::dispatch($imagePath);

                    }
                }
            }
        );

    }

}

Il toolchain node qui è dietro `lerd/fnm` e non parte nel sandbox — **il build devi lanciarlo tu**. La logica però è a posto: entrypoint `.css` → `@import` del `.scss` risolto da Tailwind (niente sass), e `viteTheme` overridato sul `.css`.

Il file dell'helper contiene import con **path assoluto** `@import '/vendor/filament/filament/resources/css/index.css'` e `/vendor/filament-themes/minimal/index.css`. namespace App\Providers\Filament;

use App\Filament\Resources\AdminResource;
use AtrioTeam\FilamentHelper\Jobs\OptimizeImage;
use AtrioTeam\FilamentHelper\PanelDefaults;
use BezhanSalleh\FilamentShield\Facades\FilamentShield;
use Filament\Panel;
use Filament\PanelProvider;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Event;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage;
use Livewire\Livewire;
use Spatie\MediaLibrary\ResponsiveImages\Events\ResponsiveImagesGeneratedEvent;

/**
 * Admin panel provider for the site.
 * Uses the default configuration from the filament-helper package.
 */
class AdminPanelProvider extends PanelProvider
{
    public function boot(): void
    {
        /**
         * this fixes the issue with nginx server, where livewire.js is not found
         * (removing the dot forces nginx to follow the route and to not serve it as static file)
         * @see https://benjamincrozat.com/livewire-js-404-not-found
         * @see https://laracasts.com/discuss/channels/livewire/has-anyone-got-livewire-3-running-in-production-on-a-nginx-server
         */
        Livewire::setScriptRoute(function ($handle) {
            // @phpstan-ignore argument.type (su $handle)
            return Route::get('/livewire/livewirejs', $handle);
        });
    }

    public function panel(Panel $panel): Panel
    {

        PanelDefaults::make($panel);

        // add further customizations here...

        /**
         * Override del tema: PanelDefaults registra il .scss dell'helper, ma Vite
         * instraderebbe i .scss al preprocessore sass (che qui non c'è). Puntiamo
         * a un entrypoint .css che importa lo stesso .scss come CSS Tailwind.
         */
        $panel->viteTheme('resources/css/filament/admin/theme.css');

        /**
         * AdminResource usa User come modello, ma i permessi Shield devono
         * usare 'Admin' come entità (non 'User') per distinguerli.
         */
        FilamentShield::buildPermissionKeyUsing(
            function (string $entity, string $affix, string $subject, string $case, string $separator): string {
                if ($entity === AdminResource::class) {
                    $subject = 'Admin';
                }

                return FilamentShield::defaultPermissionKeyBuilder(
                    affix: $affix,
                    separator: $separator,
                    subject: $subject,
                    case: $case,
                );
            }
        );

        if (config('filament-helper.tinify.enabled')) {
            $this->registerImageOptimizationJob();
        }

        return $panel;

    }

    protected function registerImageOptimizationJob(): void
    {
        Event::listen(
            ResponsiveImagesGeneratedEvent::class,
            function (ResponsiveImagesGeneratedEvent $event) {

                // loop thorught responsive images and build path for each of them, then dispatch the job to optimize the image
                foreach ($event->media->responsive_images as $conversionName) {

                    foreach ($conversionName['urls'] as $relativePath) {
                        $imagePath = Storage::disk($event->media->disk)->path(implode('/', [
                            $event->media->id,
                            'responsive-images',
                            $relativePath
                        ]));

                        OptimizeImage::dispatch($imagePath);

                    }
                }
            }
        );

    }

}

Ottima intuizione: è la strada giusta. Il `filament-helper` è **codice tuo** (working copy locale symlinkato in `vendor/` via `repositories.path`), quindi puoi editarlo e le modifiche si riflettono subito.

Il punto chiave che ho verificato: quel file **non ha vera sintassi SASS**. Niente `$variabili`, `@mixin`, `@include`, `#{}`, `@use`, `@function`. Usa solo cose che **Tailwind v4 gestisce nativamente**:
- `@import 'tailwindcss' source(none)` → sintassi Tailwind v4 (è proprio `source(none)` che sass rompe)
- `@source`, `@apply`, nesting CSS nativo

Gli **unici** due motivi per cui è costretto a passare da sass sono:
1. l'estensione `.scss`
2. **14 righe** di commenti in stile `//` (che non sono CSS valido)

## La semplificazione

Trasforma il tema helper in **CSS puro Tailwind v4**, eliminando sass del tutto:

**Nel pacchetto `filament-helper`:**
1. Rinomina `resources/theme/theme.scss` → `resources/theme/theme.css`
2. Converti i 14 commenti `// ...` → `/* ... */` (righe 2,7,63,75,76,128,129,141,142,143,147,162,210,321 — tutte a riga intera, conversione banale e sicura; l'unico `//` "a rischio" è dentro un commento a riga 129, quindi nessun problema)
3. In `PanelDefaults.php`: `->viteTheme('vendor/atrioteam/filament-helper/resources/theme/theme.css')`
4. In `DOCS/installation.md`: aggiorna il riferimento `.scss` → `.css`

**In questo progetto (atmosphera-admin):**
5. `npm uninstall sass-embedded vite-plugin-sass`
6. `vite.config.js`: rimuovi `import sass`, `sass,` dai plugin, il blocco `css.preprocessorOptions`, e punta l'input a `.../theme.css`
7. Niente override `viteTheme` (lo fa già `PanelDefaults`)

Risultato: pipeline pulita `@tailwindcss/vite`, zero toolchain sass, e ogni progetto che installa l'helper (compreso pilato quando aggiornerà Vite) non deve più portarsi dietro `sass-embedded`/`vite-plugin-sass`.

## Un'unica cosa da verificare

Pilato oggi funziona **grazie** a sass (Vite più vecchio). Convertendo il file in `.css`, il tema helper diventa universale su Vite 8; su Vite vecchio di pilato il `.css` Tailwind funziona ugualmente. Quindi la conversione **non** rompe pilato, ma andrà tolto anche lì il giro sass quando lo riallinei.

Vuoi che proceda io con la conversione nel pacchetto `filament-helper` (rename + commenti + `PanelDefaults` + docs) e poi ripulisca la config di questo progetto? Confermami e lo faccio.

# Installazione

## Pacchetto

- `composer require filament/spatie-laravel-translatable-plugin`

- `composer require awcodes/filament-sticky-header`

- `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=filament-helper-setup`

- `php artisan migrate`

- implementare in `App\Models\User` le interfacce `Filament\Models\Contracts\FilamentUser` e `Filament\Models\Contracts\HasName`, e importare il trait `\AtrioTeam\FilamentHelper\Models\IsFilamentUser`

## Permessi e autorizzazione

V. authorization.md .


## Tema

Il tema utilizzato è `vendor/atrioteam/filament-helper/resources/theme/theme.scss`, già registrato nel ServiceProvider del pacchetto:

```php
// AtrioTeam\FilamentHelper/ServiceProvider.php
// ...

$panel->viteTheme('vendor/atrioteam/filament-helper/resources/theme/theme.scss');
```

Il tema utilizza gli stili di https://filamentthemes.com/themes/minimal (registrato anche come plugin in `app/Providers/Filament/AdminPanelProvider.php`).

Il pacchetto `filament-themes/minimal` (^2.1, per Filament 5) va su un repository Composer privato, che il progetto **root** deve dichiarare — le `repositories` del composer.json di un pacchetto vengono ignorate da Composer:

```
composer config repositories.filament-themes composer https://filamentthemes.com/composer
```

Servono le credenziali di acquisto del tema (in `auth.json` non versionato, o nella variabile d'ambiente `COMPOSER_AUTH`).

Le classi utilizzate nei componenti / pagine personalizzate sono prefissate con il prefisso 'afh-' ("atrio filament helper").

## Css custom
Se è necessario un css custom per un solo progetto (aggiuntivo rispetto al tema custom già caricato):

- creare il file (es. `resources/sass/filament-custom.scss`)

- registrarlo per la compilazione in vite.config.js

- registare in un service provider, come asset aggiuntivo, l'asset di vite: (es `app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php`):

```php
use Filament\Support\Assets\Css;
use Filament\Support\Facades\FilamentAsset;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Vite;

/**
 * Custom additional css for filament
 * Register the asset only if we are not in console,
 * to avoid errors about "missing manifest" during composer install / update
 */
if (app()->runningInConsole() === false) {
    FilamentAsset::register([
        Css::make('filament-custom', Vite::asset('resources/sass/filament-custom.scss'))
    ]);
}
```

- guida base per customizzazione https://filamentphp.com/docs/3.x/support/style-customization

## Perché ora è più semplice
Il file non aveva vera sintassi SASS: gli unici ostacoli erano l'estensione `.scss` e i commenti `//`. Rimossi quelli, `@import 'tailwindcss' source(none)`, `@source`, `@apply` e il nesting sono gestiti **nativamente** da `@tailwindcss/vite`. Nessun progetto che installa l'helper deve più portarsi dietro sass.

1. **Committa il branch dell'helper** (`resources/theme/theme.css` nuovo, `theme.scss` cancellato, `PanelDefaults.php`, docs) — la sync in `vendor/` è manuale e va persa al prossimo `composer update`; con il file committato basterà un update per riallineare.
